On a frictionless horizontal surface, a constant horizontal force $F = 10\text{ N}$ acts on an object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$, moving it $4\text{ m}$. Which statement about the work $W$ done and the acceleration $a$ is correct?
20261118-physics-g05.s.s1.prompt: [E5 Physics Inquiry] Inquiry problem applying Basics of Speed. On a frictionless horizontal surface, a constant horizontal force $F = 10\text{ N}$ acts on an object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$, moving it $4\text{ m}$. Which statement about the work $W$ done and the acceleration $a$ is correct?
20261118-physics-g05.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: By Newton's second law $F = ma$, $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{10\text{ N}}{2\text{ kg}} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
Step 2: Work done is $W = F \cdot s = 10\text{ N} \times 4\text{ m} = 40\text{ J}$.
Step 3: Therefore, acceleration is $5\text{ m/s}^2$ and work done is $40\text{ J}$.
20261118-physics-g05.s.s1.hint.1: Definition of work: use $W = F \times s$.
20261118-physics-g05.s.s1.o.o0: Acceleration is $5\text{ m/s}^2$ and work done is $40\text{ J}$.
20261118-physics-g05.s.s1.o.o1: Acceleration is $2\text{ m/s}^2$ and work done is $20\text{ J}$.

20261121-physics-g05-1.title: Basics of Speed
20261121-physics-g05-1.goal: Apply principles of Basics of Speed to solve the reasoning problem.
20261121-physics-g05-1.material: [E5 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Mechanics problem analyzing Basics of Speed. An object of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest at height $h = 20\text{ m}$ in free fall ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, ignore air resistance). Which statement about mechanical energy conservation and final speed $v$ is correct?
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.prompt: [E5 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Mechanics problem analyzing Basics of Speed. An object of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest at height $h = 20\text{ m}$ in free fall ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, ignore air resistance). Which statement about mechanical energy conservation and final speed $v$ is correct?
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: With no air resistance, mechanical energy is conserved throughout fall.
Step 2: $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Step 3: $v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 20} = \sqrt{392} \approx 19.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.o.o0: Mechanical energy is conserved, and speed just before impact is approx $19.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.o.o1: Mechanical energy decreases, and speed just before impact is approx $9.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.o.o2: Only potential energy is conserved, and kinetic energy is zero.
20261121-physics-g05-1.s.s1.o.o3: Gravity varies with time, so speed cannot be calculated.

20261121-physics-g06-1.title: Electric Circuits and Lenses
20261121-physics-g06-1.goal: Apply principles of Electric Circuits and Lenses to solve the reasoning problem.
20261121-physics-g06-1.material: [E6 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Mechanics problem analyzing Electric Circuits and Lenses. An object of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest at height $h = 20\text{ m}$ in free fall ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, ignore air resistance). Which statement about mechanical energy conservation and final speed $v$ is correct?
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.prompt: [E6 Physics Inquiry (Advanced)] Mechanics problem analyzing Electric Circuits and Lenses. An object of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest at height $h = 20\text{ m}$ in free fall ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, ignore air resistance). Which statement about mechanical energy conservation and final speed $v$ is correct?
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: With no air resistance, mechanical energy is conserved throughout fall.
Step 2: $mgh = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2gh}$.
Step 3: $v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 20} = \sqrt{392} \approx 19.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.o.o0: Mechanical energy is conserved, and speed just before impact is approx $19.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.o.o1: Mechanical energy decreases, and speed just before impact is approx $9.8\text{ m/s}$.
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.o.o2: Only potential energy is conserved, and kinetic energy is zero.
20261121-physics-g06-1.s.s1.o.o3: Gravity varies with time, so speed cannot be calculated.

20261122-physics-g06-1.title: Electric Circuits and Lenses
20261122-physics-g06-1.goal: Apply principles of Electric Circuits and Lenses to solve the reasoning problem.
20261122-physics-g06-1.material: [E6 Physics Inquiry] Inquiry problem applying Electric Circuits and Lenses. On a frictionless horizontal surface, a constant horizontal force $F = 10\text{ N}$ acts on an object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$, moving it $4\text{ m}$. Which statement about the work $W$ done and the acceleration $a$ is correct?
20261122-physics-g06-1.s.s1.prompt: [E6 Physics Inquiry] Inquiry problem applying Electric Circuits and Lenses. On a frictionless horizontal surface, a constant horizontal force $F = 10\text{ N}$ acts on an object of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$, moving it $4\text{ m}$. Which statement about the work $W$ done and the acceleration $a$ is correct?
20261122-physics-g06-1.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: By Newton's second law $F = ma$, $a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{10\text{ N}}{2\text{ kg}} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
Step 2: Work done is $W = F \cdot s = 10\text{ N} \times 4\text{ m} = 40\text{ J}$.
Step 3: Therefore, acceleration is $5\text{ m/s}^2$ and work done is $40\text{ J}$.
20261122-physics-g06-1.s.s1.hint.1: Definition of work: use $W = F \times s$.
